newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court allows compounding of Reliance cases.
newsitem.headline: Indian court allows compounding of Reliance cases.

text.p: The additional chief metropolitan magistrate on Tuesday allowed Reliance Industries Ltd's plea to compound various alleged offences in a complaint filed by the Registrar of Companies (ROC), a court official said.
The magistrate also passed an order discharging Reliance, India's largest firm and its associates in 28 complaints filed by the ROC, the official said.

The Company Law Board had already passed compounding orders on 28 complaints. In the case of the 29th complaint, the Company Law Board had passed the compounding order, but the decision was subject to obtaining an order from the additional chief metropolitan magistrate.
"Now all 29 complaints stand compounded and all prosecution proceedings come to an end," the official said.
Reliance Industries, Reliance Consultancy Services and other associate firms have been directed to pay 6.39 million rupees as compounding fees, the official said.
The complaints relate to issue of duplicate shares and switching of shares lodged for registration with Reliance Consultancy Services.
Dhirubhai Ambani, the company chairman, had earlier obtained exemption from personal appearance in the court.
